tier_reason: Public Google Benchmark harness (benchmark/benchmark_algo.cpp, benchmark_function.cpp, benchmark_string.cpp, benchmark_table.cpp, benchmark_gc.cpp, benchmark_math.cpp; benchmark_common.cpp checks every iteration's result with VerifyEqual, which throws on a wrong answer) runs FakeLua JIT_GCC/JIT_TCC/JIT_INTERP against PUC Lua 5.4 in the same binary, and benchmark/README.md states GCC 15.1.0, -O3 -DNDEBUG (Release) and the CPU model (AMD EPYC 7K62) for the GCC JIT run, with full raw output. All A criteria are met; the headline ratios match the page's CPU-time rows.

corrections.claimed_speedup: JIT_GCC vs PUC Lua 5.4 (CPU-time ratios, 2026-08-14 run): Fibonacci n=32 36.6x (277.9 ms vs 7.59 ms CPU), Sum n=5M 30.4x, Popcount n=100K 37.3x, FloatPoly n=1M 34.9x, Recursion n=25 42.9x, TailRecursion n=5K 107.5x (that bench has since been removed from the harness); TCC backend Fibonacci n=32 11.2x (derived from page data: 277.9 ms vs 24.86 ms CPU). Most table and string rows are only 1.0-6.1x (TableChurn 9.3x); GCD 0.45x, ToNumber 0.53x, Variadic 0.91x and StringFind 0.85x are slower, and the Boost.Regex rows are much slower (0.06-0.21x).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Release build, -O3 -DNDEBUG (plus -g3 -fPIC from the top-level CMakeLists); GCC 15.1.0 for the JIT_GCC run, whose generated C is compiled at -O3 at script load; GCC 16.2.0 for the interpreter run. Lua baseline is the system liblua5.4 found via pkg-config (distro build flags not stated); Lua 5.4.7 is named only for the 2026-09-16 interpreter run. Google Benchmark v1.9.4.
corrections.hardware: AMD EPYC 7K62 48-Core Processor, 2-vCPU VM at 2595 MHz, load average 5.87 during the run (GCC/TCC JIT run, 2026-08-14); AMD EPYC 7551, 16-vCPU KVM (interpreter run, 2026-09-16)
corrections.caveats: Baseline is PUC Lua 5.4 (distro liblua5.4), not LuaJIT, so the result does not show a win over LuaJIT. Lua source is compiled to C and built by GCC/TCC at script load; that compile time is outside the timed region. The GCC JIT numbers come from a 2026-08-14 run on a loaded 2-vCPU cloud VM (wall times about 1.6x CPU times; the ratios use CPU time) and predate many later correctness fixes, including math-specialization eligibility fixes (commits 236a757 and 598632f, 2026-10-02); those fixes target shadowed, nested, multi-return and vararg functions that the bench scripts do not use, and the harness verifies every result, but the GCC run has not been repeated on current code. The TailRecursion bench (107.5x) was removed from the harness on 2026-09-18 (commit 12fbcd7), so that row is not reproducible from HEAD. The regex rows used Boost.Regex; commit a55a4bf (2026-10-03) implements Lua 5.4 patterns, so those rows may be obsolete. Some StringFindPattern/StringGmatch raw lines predate a workload correction (the page says so). The hand-written C++ reference column is not credible: the page says some references are folded, and C++ Sum n=5M took 27.4 ms CPU against 1.55 ms for FakeLua's GCC-compiled version of the same loop, so 'faster than C++' claims should be ignored. The bytecode interpreter tier is 1.3x to 7.6x slower than Lua 5.4 in its algorithm rows (34x on TailRecursion). Very young, fast-moving repository.

notes: Ratios check out against the raw CPU-time rows (Fib 277,915,868 ns vs 7,590,283 ns; Sum 46.98 ms vs 1.55 ms; Popcount 22.1 ms vs 0.593 ms; TailRecursion 209.8 us vs 1.95 us), but the record's '297.9 ms vs 6.8 ms' Fibonacci figures are not on the page and were corrected; the TCC 11.2x is a derived ratio. Shortcomings to record: baseline is PUC Lua not LuaJIT; GCC numbers come from an older (2026-08-14) run on a loaded 2-vCPU VM that predates later math-specialization correctness fixes (edge cases outside the bench scripts; results were verified); the TailRecursion bench was later removed; the C++ reference column is anomalous. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 214 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-10-03.

tier_reason: The README only says 'Tracing JIT with x86_64, ARM64, RISC-V backends - Faster than QEMU TCG' and the wiki Home page says emulation performance is higher than QEMU TCG thanks to the tracing RVJIT and the hardware FPU; neither gives numbers, workloads, hardware or a QEMU version, and two web searches found no published RVVM-vs-QEMU benchmark.

corrections.caveats: Tier D: bare claim in README and wiki ('Faster than QEMU TCG'; wiki credits the tracing RVJIT IR, less guest instruction splitting and use of the host hardware FPU), with no benchmark, hardware or QEMU version. A search snippet (snippet only, HN/LinuxLinks) quotes the author saying the hardware FPU path is 'like 10x faster with some synthetic FPU benchmarks', with no methodology. QEMU is not one of the listed incumbents. Licence split: librvvm MPL-2.0, rvvm and rvvm-user binaries GPL-3.0.

notes: Real, notable project (1.3k stars, active, last commit 2026-10-05), so it stays at tier D on the bare claim. Shortcoming to record: no numbers anywhere for the 'faster than QEMU TCG' claim; only a vague author quote of about 10x on synthetic FPU benchmarks (search snippet only). Licence (MPL-2.0 library, GPL-3.0 binaries) and copyable usability confirmed.
